metadata.primaryConfiguration: Libro service cutover; read and write flags independent
metadata.deploymentStatus: Vercel + Neon intended target. Production bindings are unresolved; this is not verified deployment inventory.

documents.title: Architecture and cutover
documents.text: Memorioso owns drafts, local author projections, sessions, feeds and access policy. Libro owns canonical identities and publications after cutover and uses a separate Postgres database. LIBRO_SERVICE_READS_ENABLED and LIBRO_SERVICE_WRITES_ENABLED activate independently, and only the value 1 enables either. Legacy chain-facing writes return 410 after service writes are enabled. Canonical service reads are joined to local publication_policies, preserving feed membership. Migrations 020–022 require paused canonical writes and payment settlements; never ship 020 alone. After Libro accepts writes, rollback requires a freeze and validated reverse copy, not just reversing flags. Host labels here describe logical boundaries, not provisioned infrastructure or live health.

documents.title: Identity, OAuth and extension connection
documents.text: The browser completes Libro OAuth automatically after authentication, without a separate application approval prompt. World ID verification binds the identity; handles and session IDs are lookup values, never authentication. Write grants require recent World verification. Memorioso stores OAuth tokens encrypted server-side and binds its v2 session to libro_identity_id, preserving legacy v1 world_id_session_id checks. Extension connection completes automatically after OAuth with origin and request-token checks. A short-lived polling secret delivers only an extension token; OAuth tokens never go to the extension. Discovered and dynamically registered clients do not inherit trusted author-reference namespaces.

documents.title: Browser-encrypted drafts
documents.text: An author chooses passphrase encryption or declines; unset and declined are different states. The browser seals title, subtitle and content using AES-256-GCM with draftId and userId as additional data. A v1 row contains ciphertext and null prose columns. A random per-author DEK is wrapped with a PBKDF2-SHA256-derived passphrase key and a recovery-code key. The stretched material also supplies the KEK fingerprint. IndexedDB caches a non-extractable device key, cleared at sign-out. Recovery unlock can set a new passphrase. Unavailable key-fetch, locked and declined states remain distinct. This protects data at rest, not against the server serving browser scripts. Every draft-reading surface uses revealDraftRow/revealDraftRows. Extension inline drafts use plaintext for their immediate server-driven signing flow.

documents.title: Human publication and recovery
documents.text: The author submits the exact canonical publication payload through the signing flow. IDKit publication actions are challenge-specific and bind canonical JSON as signal. The handle-bound session verifies registration via LibroRegistry.verifySession. Verification queries every configured RPC endpoint in parallel and accepts a matching registration event. Canonical content is stored in Libro; its durable outbox sends authenticated events to Memorioso, which checks pending ownership, deduplicates and updates local projections in a transaction. Prepared human operations retain operation hashes and can resume after the initial signing window without issuing a second proof. In legacy encrypted-draft publishing, browser plaintext enters the locked single-use challenge and finalize uses that stored payload; finished/abandoned challenges are swept.

documents.title: Human-authorized agents and revocation
documents.text: The handle owner authorizes an agent on chain. Agent publications use EIP-712 signatures and remain semantically separate from direct human authorship. Prepare recovers AgentDocument; finalize checks a fresh AgentDocumentFinalization signature bound to the broadcast transaction hash. Neither a document registration ID nor an app session substitutes for the agent signature. Revocation is recorded only after a matching AgentRevoked event, including service and MCP flows.

documents.title: Access policy and x402 settlement
documents.text: Gating is Memorioso presentation policy, not content confidentiality: Libro public APIs and MCP expose complete canonical signed payloads. Only articles may be gated; any authenticated Memorioso user or a settled payment grant unlocks the local view. Access policy never enters the signed signal. All Memorioso body/manifest/proof/feed surfaces apply access rules. The teaser is plain text; viewer-specific access stays outside shared caches. Missing x402 configuration removes the payment offer rather than breaking reads. Settlement uses World Chain USDC EIP-3009 and reserves a unique authorization nonce before broadcast, then records completion and the grant. X402_RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY belongs to Memorioso and remains distinct from Libro’s relayer key.

documents.title: OpenShip Sources, Systems and isolated Changes
documents.text: Discovery advertises Sources, Systems and Changes. Systems embeds exactly the same complete verified Sources snapshot plus this architecture; it is public and CORS-readable. Libro MCP remains a public Sources-only manifest/read binding. Changes is optional and returns 501 while disabled. Submitted patches target the published digest. Pure gates run in the API and again in the worker; build, review and deployment gates follow. The resulting source digest determines buildId. Submitted code executes in a container without production secrets and without network after installation. VERCEL_TOKEN stays in the trusted worker and is passed only to deploy prebuilt output, which does not execute submitted code. Review and path filters are not the security boundary. Candidate domains must have a separate registrable domain, including from production siblings. A ready preview is never automatic production promotion.

documents.title: Deployment and source maintenance
documents.text: Memorioso and Libro are separate Next.js applications and databases. Shared core, Chrome extension and Foundry contracts have separate checks. Database pools are lazy and build-time reads have missing-database fallbacks. Only Libro receives WORLD_ID_RP_SIGNING_KEY and LIBRO_RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY after cutover; Memorioso retains its session secret, encrypted client tokens and x402 relayer. Environment names may be published; values and credentials are not. Keep this model in the source snapshot, update it alongside architecture changes, and validate it against the published Sources. Structural checks do not establish semantic accuracy or live service availability.

documents.title: Memorioso logical data model
documents.text: Authors own drafts. Drafts contain either encrypted content with null prose fields or opted-out prose. Local author projections, publication policies and feed membership remain local even when canonical publication data comes from Libro. Payment grants belong to local access policy. OAuth tokens are encrypted. No production records or required seed records are supplied.

documents.title: Libro logical data model
documents.text: Canonical identities own canonical publications. Human and agent signatures remain distinct proof classes. OAuth grants and tokens are identity-scoped; signing challenges bind exact operations. Durable outbox events synchronize consumers. Libro uses a database separate from Memorioso. No production records or required seed records are supplied.
